correctness.rationale: The rotor-on-tree frontier induction forces parent-directed earlier spine rotors at each new frontier. Each stage traverses at most twice the 2j+1 edges of the rooted comb prefix plus its exit edge; equality requires a fresh rotor pointing to the next spine vertex. On first reaching the far endpoint the chip lies on the unique rotor dimer and is recurrent. The extremal end-leaf dimer prevents earlier recurrence. Initial terminal leftward orientation produces earlier recurrence, proving uniqueness. This exact all-n proof agrees with exhaustive tests through 12 spine vertices.

value.rationale: The sharp maximal deterministic first-recurrence time and its unique realizing rotor assignment are natural invariants of a bounded-degree finite comb tree, quantifying the effect of pendant-leaf memory on exploration delay. The exact quadratic leading coefficient and uniqueness are not inferred from generic O(mD) bounds. The directed-frontier tour mechanism motivates future extremal comparisons for decorated trees.
